verdict: MU blowout Q3 ($41.5B +346% YoY, Q4 guided $50B); SK Hynix pivots HBM4 capacity to DDR5 (margins ~90%); OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC launched — memory supercycle confirmed mid-cycle, custom silicon accelerating.

## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing (ACCELERATING):** TrendForce confirmed Q1-2026 conventional DRAM +93-98% QoQ (industry revenue +81% QoQ to $97B). Q2-2026: conv DRAM +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ — moderating from Q1 record pace but still historically extreme. June 22 TrendForce note: consumers now diverting to legacy DDR2/DDR3 due to shortages; DDR2 prices +55-60% QoQ forecast in 3Q26. HBM contract prices slightly declined due to annual pricing mechanisms, but TrendForce (June 2) now projects HBM prices to "surge multiples higher in 2027" as generation transitions tighten supply.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk (MIXED):** TrendForce (June 23) flagged a strategic split: Samsung HBM4 revenue reportedly tops $1B; SK Hynix deliberately SLOWING its HBM4 ramp — converting HBM3E lines to DDR5 instead. DDR5 operating margins approaching 90% make conventional DRAM more immediately lucrative. SK Hynix signed a 3-year DDR5 LTA with Microsoft. SK Hynix briefly displaced Samsung as South Korea's most valuable company (June 22) before both fell ~12% (June 23). Net effect: HBM4 capacity additions may arrive slower than feared, potentially pushing out the "correction after 2026" timeline.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex (ABOVE BASELINE):** No fresh prints in last 24-72h. Running total: MSFT+GOOGL+AMZN+META collectively guiding $725B capex in 2026 (+77% YoY), above baseline's $600-700B upper end. NVDA Q1 FY27 data center revenue was a record $75.2B (+92% YoY). No guide-downs visible.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400/Helios + Custom ASICs (KEY NEW CATALYST):** AMD MI400/Helios confirmed on-track for 2H-2026; AMD July "Advancing AI" event flagged for detail. CRITICAL: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled "Jalapeño," OpenAI's first custom AI ASIC — the first foundation-model lab owning its own silicon at this scale, a landmark signal for the custom-silicon displacement thesis. Custom ASICs growing 44.6% vs 16.1% for standard GPUs in 2026. Google Ironwood (TPU v7) GA'd in April; Meta unveiled MTIA 300-500 roadmap through 2027; AWS Trainium4 announced for late 2026/early 2027.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics (DIPPING, STRUCTURALLY INTACT):** Both COHR and LITE pulled back >15% from early-June peaks after triple-digit YTD gains. J.P. Morgan reiterated Overweight on both (COHR PT $380, LITE PT $1,130), calling the dip a buying opportunity and flagging non-NVIDIA CSP demand as "additive to current forecasts." Coherent signed LOI for up to $50M direct funding (June 16). Lumentum received the largest single CPO laser purchase commitment in its history. InP supply constraints and CPO 0-to-1 trajectory unchanged.

**Signal 6 — Solar (POLICY TAIL WIND BUILDING):** Solar stocks +40% YTD. FSLR volatile: Supreme Court struck down IEEPA-based reciprocal tariffs — structurally positive (lower import duties on unfinished goods, shifts production to U.S. at higher ASPs). UBS raised FSLR PT to $330 on June 11 (+9% day). Section 232 tariff decision still pending as the next major catalyst. NXT remains broadly constructive. No fresh module/polysilicon data in last 24h.

## Context vs Baseline

- **DRAM pricing:** Tracking above baseline. Q1 actuals (+93-98%) hit the high end of baseline's +90-95% forecast. Q2 decelerating to +58-63% but cumulative H1 effect has more than doubled conv DRAM prices.
- **HBM correction risk:** SK Hynix's DDR5 pivot is a mild counter — if three suppliers don't all ramp HBM4 aggressively, the feared 2027 glut may be pushed out. But the baseline warning stands; watch Samsung's 250K wafer/month HBM target.
- **Hyperscaler capex:** $725B exceeds baseline's $600-700B upper bound. Structural demand floor is rising.
- **Custom ASICs:** OpenAI Jalapeño accelerates the thesis beyond the baseline's "1/3 of compute by 2030" — a top-3 model lab now owns its own silicon by mid-2026.
- **Optical:** Short-term dip vs baseline's supply-shortage structural thesis; JPM calling it a buying opportunity is consistent with baseline.

## Most Important Development

**Micron's record Q3 ($41.5B revenue +346% YoY, Q4 guided $50B at 86% GM)** is the biggest single data point: it confirms the memory supercycle is mid-cycle, not peaking, and provides a concrete earnings anchor for the bull thesis. A close second: **SK Hynix's strategic pivot away from HBM4 toward DDR5** — DDR5 margins approaching 90% are pulling capacity away from HBM4 ramp, both delaying the feared oversupply glut and illustrating just how extreme the broader DRAM pricing environment has become. Third: **OpenAI + Broadcom Jalapeño** — a foundation-model lab owning its own silicon by mid-2026 meaningfully accelerates the custom-ASIC narrative ahead of schedule.

Not investment advice. Forward figures are forecasts.
